body:
MYK'S QUESTION (2026-07-26): does the hex string grow with the complexity of the hyperview? MEASURED ANSWER, from the code: yes, linearly, because neither field is a hash. `viewCanonicalHex(v)` and `hviewCanonicalHex(h)` (rhizomatic) hex-encode the CBOR CANONICAL FORM — the comment says it plainly, "same (schema, DSet) => byte-identical form": the FORM is the address. So `_hex` is 2 hex chars per CBOR byte of the VIEW — a pick-latest view over a million-delta bucket stays tiny, but an `all`/`conflicts` policy or a wide props map makes `_hex` as large as the answer itself, tripling every response that requests it (data + its re-serialization, hexed). And `_hviewHex` serializes THE ENTIRE GATHERED BUCKET — on a million-delta hyperview that is the million deltas, in hex, per request. The operator-review postcard (3 props) already produced a ~230-char `_hex` with the field values legible inside it — which is also a quiet INFORMATION LEAK: `_hex` on a public door re-discloses every resolved value even if a client displays only one field (minor today since the door serves the fields anyway, but it forecloses ever serving a projection).

NOTE the substrate is not confused: delta ids ARE digests (`computeId = contentAddress(canonicalBytes)`, fixed 68 chars). The view/hview fields just never got the same treatment, and rhizomatic is FROZEN — but no substrate change is needed: Loam's surface can hash the canonical bytes itself (`contentAddress(bytes)` is already exported) and keep every equality property, since digest equality ⇔ byte equality for the comparisons every consumer actually makes (the tutorial finale's _hex-for-_hex, SSE's _fromHex→_hex frames, claims.test's shared-_hviewHex, the operator review's convergence check).

THE DECISION (Myk's — this changes what the API promises): (a) make `_hex`/`_hviewHex` fixed-size digests of the canonical bytes (64 hex chars), breaking any consumer that PARSES the hex (audit says: none in-tree — every use is equality); (b) add `_digest`/`_hviewDigest` beside the old fields and deprecate growth; or (c) keep bytes and document the cost. Recommend (a): fixed-size, same semantics, closes the leak, shrinks SSE frames — with a §17 spec correction and the tutorial finale re-verified. No §20 migration: these fields are computed at read time, never at rest.

RAILS when built: digest stability across arrival orders (the existing read tests re-aimed); the SSE frame carries fixed-width hashes; a probe that the old legible-values property is GONE (the leak closed is an assertable absence: the hex no longer contains the view's strings).

DECIDED AND PRIORITIZED (Myk, 2026-07-26): "let's lock this down sooner than later, this is a priority and having those unbounded hex strings is gonna blow up in our face immediately." Option (a) is CHOSEN — `_hex` and `_hviewHex` become fixed-size digests of the canonical bytes. Build now, ahead of the queue. The PR still stops for Myk (API promise change) but the direction is settled; do not re-litigate it in P1.

BUILD CARE, from the pre-audit: (1) grep every consumer of `viewCanonicalHex`/`hviewCanonicalHex` — the SURFACE fields digest, but any INTERNAL use as a memo/materialization key may stay bytes or digest freely (equality preserved either way); (2) the one sharp edge is `derivedClaims(..., inputHex)` — if a derivation records the full canonical hex as provenance IN AT-REST DELTAS, digesting changes newly-derived delta ids for identical inputs, so a pre-change and post-change derivation of the same input would coexist as duplicates. Audit that path FIRST and state the finding either way; if it bites, the fix is scoped there (keep derivation-internal identity as-is, or accept and document the one-time re-derivation) — never a silent skip. (3) The capabilities book's chapter 2 says a query answers with "a hash of it" — today that sentence overclaims and T107 makes it true; note it in the PR. (4) The renderer floor exposes `n.hex` and pages slice it for display — a 64-char digest slices fine, but re-run the site suites.
title: `_hex` and `_hviewHex` are canonical BYTES, not digests — the identity fields grow with the answer, and the hyperview one grows with the bucket
